# DocumentSettings

<!-- Generated from the doc comments in the library. Do not edit this file. -->

Configures document-wide page, output, security, accessibility, and metadata behavior.

Import from `@bonniepdf/core`.

## Constructors

```typescript
new DocumentSettings()
new DocumentSettings(pageSize: PdfSize, margin: number)
new DocumentSettings(pageSize: PdfSize, orientation: PageOrientation, margin: number)
new DocumentSettings(pageSize: PdfSize, orientation: PageOrientation)
new DocumentSettings(options: DocumentSettingsOptions)
```

### `accessibility`

```typescript
accessibility: AccessibilityMode
```

Accessibility (tagging) mode. Accepts `'none' | 'pdf/ua-1' | 'pdf/ua-2'`.

Example, from `code-recipes/barcodes-qr-codes/barcodes`:

```typescript
settings.accessibility = AccessibilityMode.PdfUa1;
```

### `bookmarks`

```typescript
bookmarks: BookmarkItem[]
```

Gets or sets the bookmark items for the document outline tree.

> A list you can change.

Example, from `industry-templates/people-hr/employment-contract`:

```typescript
settings.bookmarks = [
  new BookmarkItem({ title: 'Particulars', pageIndex: pages.particulars }),
  new BookmarkItem({ title: 'Definitions', pageIndex: pages.definitions }),
  new BookmarkItem({
    title: 'Clauses',
    pageIndex: pages.clauses[0] ?? 0,
    children: data.clauses.map(
      (c, i) => new BookmarkItem({ title: `${i + 1}. ${c.heading}`, pageIndex: pages.clauses[i] ?? 0 })
    ),
  }),
  new BookmarkItem({ title: 'Schedule 1 — Benefits and allowances', pageIndex: pages.schedule }),
  new BookmarkItem({ title: 'Execution', pageIndex: pages.execution }),
];
```

### `defaultTextStyle`

```typescript
defaultTextStyle?: TextStyle | undefined
```

*optional*

Default text style applied to all text elements that have not had their style properties explicitly set. Use this to define a document-wide font/size/color baseline and avoid repeating style assignments on every element.

```typescript
doc.settings.defaultTextStyle = new TextStyle()
  .withFamily('Helvetica')
  .withSize(11)
  .withColor(ColorPalette.slate[600]);
```

Example, from `code-recipes/text-styling/text-alignment`:

```typescript
settings.defaultTextStyle = new TextStyle()
```

Example, from `industry-templates/retail-events/edge-receipt`:

```typescript
settings.defaultTextStyle = new TextStyle().withFamily('Courier').withSize(9).withColor(INK);
```

### `facturX`

```typescript
facturX?: FacturXMetadata | undefined
```

*optional*

ZUGFeRD / Factur-X e-invoice metadata. When set (and the document is a PDF/A-3 level), the XMP writer emits the `fx:*` conformance block. Normally set via [`applyFacturX`](apply-factur-x.md) rather than directly — that helper also attaches the XML and forces PDF/A-3. Default `undefined`.

### `footerTemplate`

```typescript
footerTemplate?: PageTemplate | undefined
```

*optional*

Template function for generating page footers. Called with the page number (1-based) and should return an IElement to render at the bottom of each page. The returned element is rendered at the bottom margin position.

Example, from `code-recipes/compliance-archival/pdf-compliance`:

```typescript
settings.footerTemplate = pageTemplate({ default: footer });
```

Example, from `code-recipes/comparison-charts/bar-chart`:

```typescript
settings.footerTemplate = pageTemplate({ default: pageFooter() });
```

### `language`

```typescript
language?: string | undefined
```

*optional*

Document natural language as a BCP-47 tag (e.g. `"en-GB"`, `"de-DE"`, `"fr"`). Written to the catalog as `/Lang` when set; required for PDF/UA-1 conformance, where it tells assistive tech the language of unmarked content. Default `undefined` (no language declared).

Example, from `industry-templates/invoices/factur-x-invoice`:

```typescript
settings.language = 'en';
```

Example, from `code-recipes/barcodes-qr-codes/barcodes`:

```typescript
settings.language = 'en-GB';
```

### `maxImageDpi`

```typescript
maxImageDpi: number | null
```

The most pixels per inch an embedded PNG image is kept at (default: 288). An image that carries more pixels than its printed size can use is reduced to this resolution when the document is written, by an exact area average that never re-encodes the image lossily and never enlarges it. `null` embeds every image at its source resolution. JPEG, indexed and 16-bit images are always embedded as they are; `Document.diagnostics` reports what was reduced and what was passed through.

### `missingGlyphs`

```typescript
missingGlyphs: MissingGlyphs | "drop" | "throw"
```

What happens to a character no registered font can draw: `'drop'` (the default) leaves it out and records a `font` warning; `'throw'` stops generation with a `MissingGlyphException`. A character that falls back to another font is not missing.

```typescript
namedDestinations: Map<string, number>
```

### `orientation`

```typescript
orientation: PageOrientation
```

Page orientation. Accepts `'portrait' | 'landscape'`.

Example, from `code-recipes/share-ranking-charts/pie-chart`:

```typescript
settings.orientation = PageOrientation.Landscape;
```

### `oversizedContent`

```typescript
oversizedContent: "throw" | OversizedContent | "clip"
```

What happens to content that cannot split across pages and is taller than a page: `'clip'` (the default) draws it at the top of a page, cut off at the bottom of the body, and records an error diagnostic; `'throw'` stops generation with an `OversizedContentError`. Text, tables, lists and stacks split instead, so they are never oversized.

### `pageBackground`

```typescript
pageBackground?: PageTemplate | undefined
```

*optional*

Template function for the full-page **background** slot. Called with the page number (1-based); the returned element is painted *behind* all page content. Unlike `headerTemplate` / `footerTemplate`, the background slot spans the **entire page and ignores the margins**, so bleed images, scanned letterhead, and certificate backgrounds reach the page edge. Rendered at the page origin (0, 0) with the full page width available.

Example, from `industry-templates/retail-events/event-ticket`:

```typescript
settings.pageBackground = pageTemplate({ default: pageBackdrop() });
```

Example, from `industry-templates/finance-reporting/annual-report`:

```typescript
settings.pageBackground = (pageNumber: number): IElement => (pageNumber === 1 ? coverBackground() : pageBands());
```

### `pageColor`

```typescript
pageColor: Color | undefined
```

Page background fill. Accepts a palette token or hex.

Example, from `industry-templates/education-public-sector/grant-award-letter`:

```typescript
settings.pageColor = Color.white;
```

### `pageForeground`

```typescript
pageForeground?: PageTemplate | undefined
```

*optional*

Template function for the full-page **foreground** slot. Called with the page number (1-based); the returned element is painted *on top of* all page content (including headers and footers), making it ideal for "DRAFT"/"CONFIDENTIAL" overlays and stamps. Like `pageBackground` it spans the entire page and ignores the margins, rendered at the page origin (0, 0) with the full page width available.

### `pageLabel`

```typescript
pageLabel?: PageLabel | undefined
```

*optional*

Page labelling configuration written as `/PageLabels` in the document catalog (PDF §12.4.2). Controls the number shown in the viewer's page counter and "go to page" dialog — not the printed text on the page itself.

Use when the document represents a subset of a larger work and the viewer counter should reflect the logical page numbering rather than the physical 1-based sheet count.

```typescript
const label = new PageLabel()
label.startAt = 42
settings.pageLabel = label
// → viewer shows "42" on page 1, "43" on page 2, etc.
```

Note: the footer template still receives the physical page number. Offset it manually if you want the printed number to match: `footerTemplate = (n) => new TextBlock(String(n + 41))`

Example, from `code-recipes/long-form-typesetting/book-page-layout`:

```typescript
settings.pageLabel = pageLabel;
```
